title: The Hajj verses
hookLine: the pilgrimage, the months, no quarreling, remember Allah at Arafat (2:196–203)

lines: A CROWD ON ANOTHER SCALE, IN THE HEAT.
cards: A stadium letting out. A train station at rush hour. An airport the day before a holiday.

Crowds like that test anyone's patience, and the Hajj is a crowd on another scale: pilgrims from far-off countries, in the heat, old and young, all trying to reach the same few places on the same days.
Tempers can fray anywhere. In the middle of its laws for this journey, al-Baqarah sets a rule about tempers. Today: the Hajj verses.

teach.h: A SHORT HANDBOOK FOR THE PILGRIMAGE
teach.b: Verses one hundred ninety-six to two hundred three are a short handbook for the pilgrimage. Complete the Hajj and the 'umrah for God. The pilgrimage is in the well-known months.
Then verse one hundred ninety-seven: whoever takes on the Hajj in them, let there be no indecent talk, no wrongdoing, and no quarreling on the Hajj.
The word for quarreling is jidal: arguing, disputing, wrestling with words. It's named where arguments come easily: over a spot in the tent, a push in the crowd, who was first in line.

teach.h: NO INDECENCY, NO WRONG, NO QUARREL
teach.b: A hadith in Bukhari says whoever performs the Hajj without indecency or wrongdoing returns as on the day their mother bore them.
Then the verse turns practical: take provisions for the journey, and the best provision is taqwa, the mindfulness you met on the first page of al-Baqarah.
The next verse adds: there is no sin in seeking the bounty of your Lord, which the commentators say means trading during the pilgrimage season. Ordinary life isn't banned. Quarreling is.
Then the heart of it: when you press on from Arafat, remember God at the sacred landmark. Arafat is a plain outside Mecca where pilgrims spend one day standing in prayer.
A hadith in at-Tirmidhi says simply: the Hajj is Arafah. The day at the center of the journey is spent remembering, not winning arguments.

how: Muslims who are able perform the Hajj once in a lifetime in the month of Dhul-Hijjah; pilgrims enter a state of ihram, avoid quarreling and indecent speech, and spend the Day of Arafah standing in prayer on the plain of Arafat.

o: the pushing and crowding of pilgrims
the stoning of the pillars on the Hajj

games.q: the pilgrim's handbook — tap the pairs.

s: al-Baqarah forbids all trade during the Hajj season
2:198: no sin in seeking your Lord's bounty, which commentators read as trade.
the Hajj verses name quarreling as something to avoid
no indecent talk, no wrongdoing, no quarreling on the Hajj.
a hadith says the Hajj is Arafah
at-Tirmidhi: the day of standing is the heart of it.

games.q: you're on the Hajj, exhausted, and someone pushes ahead of you in the crowd. what does verse 197 say?
games.why: no quarreling: the rule is set right where arguments come easily, and the best provision for the road is taqwa.

practice: Picture where today's arguments are likely to start, a family member, a colleague, a comment thread, traffic, and the moment one begins.
Then picture letting the other person have the last word, not because they're right, but because you're on a journey and this isn't what you're carrying.

wordCard.voice: Jidal. Quarreling, disputing, wrestling with words — the one thing al-Baqarah forbids on the Hajj, in a crowd where tempers fray easily. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: quarreling, disputing; in 2:197, no jidal on the Hajj.

carryVoice: Your line: no quarrel on the journey. The best provision is taqwa. Day three hundred fifty-four, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1521 (returns as on the day his mother bore him)
